#1702. Zubimendi addresses tiredness and transfer talk

Good morning all, hope you’re well! It’s St. Martin’s Day in Germany, a day I’d never heard of until I had a child over here. Kids will leave Kindergarten and chant as they walk through their neighbourhoods with lanterns this evening, as is tradition. Doesn’t sound creepy at all, does it?

St. Martin was, as the story goes, a 4th-Century Roman soldier and is best known for sharing his cloak with a freezing beggar.

Fitting, then, that Martin Zubimendi should be linked with a move to Chelsea (and others). It would be the saintly thing to do to share some of our midfield spoils with the desperate, downtrodden, shivering squad that Xabi Alonso has at his disposal. I hope we let them get absolutely glacial – Siberian, even, given their history – and keep our glorious cloak of midfielders all to ourselves.

The first rule of the international break is, of course, to ignore all transfer rumours. Club football goes away but there are still pages to fill, newspapers to sell, online traffic to amass, and something has to fill the void.

And, speaking to Marca, the midfielder has denied that he’s unhappy:

I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. (Not playing) is something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.

Asked about the toll that playing so much took on him last season – Zubimendi was the only Arsenal player to play in all 38 Premier League games, he started 34 of those and had the third most minutes in the squad, behind David Raya and Declan Rice, across all competitions – he admitted that that was a factor:

I don’t like to blame everything on my physical condition, but I definitely noticed it that year. It was a new year for me, with a lot of new stimuli. I played a huge number of minutes and, to be honest, I was tired. Then there were other things too, but one of them could very well have been my physical condition.

I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me. He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

And he completely dismissed any suggestion that he is talking to other clubs, given those links to the Madrid sides and Chelsea:

I haven’t wasted any energy on outside things. I’m busy enough trying to earn a place, get playing time, and fight to win this Premier League, which is looking so promising. I haven’t spent any energy on it, nor have I contacted anyone.

To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish. Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close (to a transfer), but not at all.

Still, I do think the case of Zubimendi is an interesting one. Having lost his place late last season, he returned late in the summer, and is yet to start a Premier League game in 2026-27 following the emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly and the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes.

Here we have a player Arsenal desperately wanted and agreed a deal for a year ahead of signing him, would they really be looking to move him on again now that he’s spent what is essentially just a quarter of a season not as first choice? So much focus has been placed on building a squad that can sustain injuries or absences, and then we’d leave ourselves light again?

Maybe? You never can know how transfers pan out ahead of time, and things can change quickly in football but, as Zubimendi suggests, they can change quickly in the other direction again too. Did anyone, for instance, envisage Lewis-Skelly starting against Atletico Madrid just a week before it actually happened?

I do think his particular rise, and a stressful second half of the season, has clouded what we all thought of Zubimendi’s first half-season at Arsenal, and how much he contributed across the entire campaign. At this stage a year ago, we were two points worse off than we are now but still top of the league by six points, with more goals scored and fewer goals conceded than we are 10 games in this time around. He was a big part of that.

He was a huge part of winning the title and reaching the Champions League final – he started 43 of our 53 games across those two competitions. He started every Champions League knockout game up until the semi-final second leg and played all of extra-time in the final.

And if he was suffering physically, there was no break in the summer, as he went off to the World Cup, Spain went all the way, and he was back on the pitch for Arsenal (having had no pre-season) in Cardiff as we won the Community Shield, less than a month on from the World Cup final.

For all that, I can also see why someone would possibly want to make the case for moving on. Seeing a player not be used (Zubimendi has played in seven of our league games so far this season, by the way!) feels like an obvious place to upgrade, and we’ve been scarred before by letting players sit on the bench before then struggling to move them on for a fair fee.

We’re also going to need to refresh the age of the team and especially the midfield before long. When you don’t just look at the players themselves but actually account for who is playing the minutes, we have the third-oldest squad in the league this season. The frontline will need new faces soon – that’s not news to anyone – in terms of age as well as quality, but the midfield will need it on the age front as well.

We’ve also given the fewest minutes in the league to players under the age of 23 (around 6%) by some distance. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it, but if you don’t get the balance right it will break in time.

Right now, though, this season, we’re likely to need our whole squad. We can’t be making it weaker. If one of Declan Rice – God forbid – or Bruno Guimaraes were to pick up a knock and miss a month, Zubimendi would suddenly be in line for a lot of football. Zubimendi who, again, was central to us winning the league last season.

It’s far too soon into the season to write his campaign off, especially when we saw how things changed so suddenly in that exact position back in May. Let’s see how things look when the summer rolls around, but there’s no need to rush into a decision.

Right then, have a great day all – and I’ll leave you with the gorgeous generosity of another St. Martin close to our hearts.

In the summer, Palladino turned down a long-term contract with Atalanta because he was linked with more prestigious jobs, but this left him without a job. Then, when Bologna parted ways with Domenico Tedesco, the Italian took his talents to Reggio Emilia and has not looked back.

#1700. The virtues of patience

It’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

It was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

This was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

By then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

Come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

The Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he says he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he said, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, says the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

“The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

“Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”

To be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and new faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

Ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.

#1699. Next Man United manager: Thoughts of Red Devils dressing room on potential Unai Emery arrival 'revealed'

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 16:46, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 16:49

A number of Manchester United players had allegedly been hoping that the club would appoint Unai Emery as their next head coach.

Michael Carrick is expected to be sacked by the 20-time English champions, with an announcement from the club potentially coming on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino, who is in charge of the United States, is set to be appointed as the club's new head coach once Carrick's exit has been confirmed.

However, according to talkSPORT, a number of Man United players had been hoping that the club would bring in Emery as their next manager.

Emery is admired by senior figures at Man United, but the Spaniard is in discussions with Aston Villa over a new long-term contract.

The 55-year-old's existing deal is due to run until June 2029, but an announcement over an extension is expected in the not too distant future.

Earlier this month, Emery revealed that discussions were taking place over keeping him at Villa Park on an even longer basis.

"My ambition is to keep our consistency and how we are improving and building lots of things positively. It is a huge challenge," the Villa boss told reporters.

"They decided, speaking with us last year, to build a new stand to add more supporters at Villa Park. That is a clear step forward to get better.

"How we are increasing our budget each year, and revenue through our performance by playing in Europe and improving players, selling players, then buying young talented players, this is the process and ambition we should keep in the future.

"I had a good meeting with Nassef Sawiris, very good meeting, very positive. Let's talk next week, trying to get everything we spoke about together. We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a deal, yes."

Man United faced Villa in the Premier League last time out, twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Emery's side at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils will return to action against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22, and the expectation is that Pochettino will be in charge for that contest.

#1698. Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

Chelsea had looked down and out, when, just three minutes after Alonso’s quadruple half-time change, Leeds doubled their lead. But four goals in an incredible 12-minute spell turned the tie on its head and it was Alonso’s substitutes who Chelsea had to thank.

Palmer, with some help from Gillett, was the first to come to the home side’s rescue. Four minutes after Brenden Aaronson had put Leeds 2-0 up, Gillett pointed to the penalty spot after Daniel James had stood on the foot of Pep Chavarría.

It looked like a harsh decision on Leeds and proved to be almost as big of a game-changer as Alonso’s substitutions. Palmer stepped up to score the resulting penalty.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

“Nobody in the stadium, not one player was asking for a penalty and he gave the penalty,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “All of a sudden their players came into the game. The momentum was on their side. Situations can change the whole momentum of the game.”

Stamford Bridge sensed a comeback and in the 55th minute, Rogers nudged the ball into the path of Palmer who produced a brilliant curling finish to beat Michael Zetterer, the Leeds goalkeeper.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Reece James then went close, before Neto completed the turnaround on the hour mark. Palmer found Rogers, who in turn picked out Neto and he sent Stamford Bridge wild by sending his shot into the corner of the net.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

As Farke waited to make a quadruple substitution of his own, Danny Welbeck got in on the act by collecting the ball from Rogers, spinning and scoring.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

That should have been that and the atmosphere could not have been more different from half-time, when Chelsea fans had booed off their side after watching them fall a goal behind.

Reggie Watson, Chelsea’s 16-year-old debutant, Malo Gusto, Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens were hooked at half-time by Alonso, who said: “For sure, I take responsibility for all of them. No player to blame. It’s the decisions that we took.

“I know that probably I haven’t taken the right decisions for them to show their best level. It’s something that I will analyse and learn from. So it’s my responsibility and we had to make decisions at half-time. And we have seen another second half with another quality.”

Goalkeeper Mike Penders was one of the nine changes made by Alonso. He produced a superb double-save to first keep out Aaronson and then recover to tip Tarik Muharemovic’s header out from the corner.

Conor Coady was impressed with that Mike Penders double save in the first half 👏 pic.twitter.com/6NJqFDvnzk

But the Belgian flapped at the corner, which gave Harry Wilson a second chance to get his delivery right. And he did just that by finding Muharemovic at the back post to head the ball into the net.

Valentín Barco survived Alonso’s changes, but was partly at fault for Leeds’s second goal just after the break. He lost the ball and Ethan Ampadu galloped away from Rogers before crossing. Lukas Nmecha got the slightest of touches and Aaronsen smashed the ball into the net.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

The substitutes then took over, as Chelsea shocked the visitors before Leeds substitute Dominic Calvert-Lewin gave his team hope by reducing the deficit with 15 minutes remaining.

Any thoughts of a Leeds comeback were quickly erased, however, as Barco netted his first Chelsea goal from a Rogers pass, which may have taken a slight touch to deny him a fourth assist in the record books. Welbeck added a sixth in time added on.

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

On the defeat by Chelsea, Farke said: “The referee had the idea to give a penalty. No one in the stadium was asking for it, no one of their players was asking for it, but he spotted a situation where he thought he would give a penalty.

“All of a sudden they scored the goal, then their players came into the game at half-time, the whole stadium after being relatively quiet for 60 minutes they of course were there then. The momentum was all of a sudden on their side. In football small situations can change the whole momentum of a game and this happened.”

"100% I meant it!" 😅Morgan Rogers says he is really enjoying his football after he helped Chelsea beat Leeds 6-3 in the Carabao Cup! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/7uUQb6eIla

Here’s a reminder of the assist in question. Did Rogers mean it? Let us know in the comments beneath this live blog...

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

"Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk

On the message from the manager at half-time, Palmer told Sky Sports: “Just up the intensity, play a bit more, become more alive because I think the first half was flat, everyone agreed in the changing room, so we stepped up.

Asked whether Alonso’s message was delivered calmly, he said: “At the start, but then he got a bit angry. But it was alright.”

On Chelsea’s half-time changes, Conor Coady said on Sky Sports: “I think the credit goes down to [Alonso]. He made a bit of a statement by doing that at half-time. Four subs is a lot to do at half-time but it was needed. Listen, we said about the first half that it was kind of like the players hadn’t played with each other, and then the big guns came on... They were electric at times.”

A crazy match which was decided by Chelsea’s superb substitutes. Alonso took action at half-time and was rewarded with six goals in a madcap second half. Palmer hauled Chelsea back into the game, Rogers collected a handful of assists and Neto scored the go-ahead goal. You wonder what this match will do for the likes of Estevao and Gittens, though.

Chelsea 6 Leeds United 3 (Welbeck) Pure reflexes from Welbeck, who diverts Barco’s wild effort beyond Zetterer.

Palmer has the hat-trick ball on his mind and attempts an audacious chip but just gets his angles wrong. Any guesses who laid on the chance? Rogers. Of course.

Fans in the away end have resolved they have seen enough and are now heading towards the exits. Stach attempts to launch a counter but his raking cross-field ball is far too heavy.

Rogers drifts out to the left and wins Chelsea a valuable corner. James walks over to take it to rapturous applause from supporters there.

Leeds look to break but Wilson mistimes his run and is caught offside.

There will be six minutes of time added on.

Chance! Okafor darts inside of Neto and spins in a teasing ball to the back post but neither Calvert-Lewin nor Tanaka are able to reach it.

Shouts for a Leeds penalty fail to pique the interest of referee Gillett. Gudmundsson was felled on the left of the box but the contact looked minimal.

A tap on Barco’s head from Wilson provokes some histrionics from the Argentine but Jarred Gillett calms all parties down.

Leeds are still pushing. Stach’s effort from eight yards out is closed down before Tanaka’s strike from the edge of the box is smothered by James.

Alonso goes into the book, apparently for straying too far outside of his technical area.

Chelsea 5 Leeds United 3 (Barco) Rogers lays on his fourth assist of the match, driving towards the byline before flashing a searching ball across the face of goal which Barco spears past Zetterer at the far post. That should be that, right?

Valentín Barco gets Chelsea a FIFTH! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/XnhgvhBpL9

Gudmundsson replaces debutant Bard down Leeds’ left.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 3 (Calvert-Lewin) Game back on? Okafor is afforded far too much space down the left by a tiring Chelsea back line and his cross finds Calvert-Lewin who plants the ball past Penders to reduce the deficit to just one goal. What a tie this has turned into!

Leeds win a corner, which falls to Stach on the edge of the box but his effort is charged down.

It will be a source of acute anguish for Farke that Chelsea’s fourth goal came before he could make his four changes: Stach, Calvert-Lewin, Tanaka and Okafor eventually replace James, Nmecha, Longstaff and Aaronson. Conversely, it should be to Alonso’s credit that he took action early - his substitutes have decided this tie.

Chelsea 4 Leeds United 2 (Welbeck) Rogers gallops on to a simple ball down the right channel and his cutback (towards Palmer) is picked up by Welbeck who spins before firing beyond Zetterer, leaving three Leeds defenders sprawled in front of him. He cares not, and absorbs the love of the crowd in the near corner.

Class from Danny Welbeck 😤 pic.twitter.com/FUFKxlzXDz

Palmer goes close after having found a yard of space on the edge of the box. His strike spears through a thicket of limbs in Leeds’ box but Zetterer pulls off a strong save to deny the Englishman a quickfire hat-trick.

Chelsea 3 Leeds United 2 (Neto) Just 11 minutes after going 2-0 down, Chelsea find themselves ahead. Palmer threads a through-ball through the middle for Rogers, who slides in front of his marker to an open Neto who sweeps the ball beyond Zetterer. Leeds punished for leaving themselves two vs two at the back there.

"This is a comeback of comebacks!" Pedro Neto scores and Chelsea have turned it around eleven minutes after going 2-0 down! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/FTPuWcFqEX

Chelsea have got their tails up and Palmer almost lays on a go-ahead goal but James cannot turn in his cross from the left.

Chelsea 2 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Wow! Palmer has turned this game on its head. And it’s so, so simple. Acheampong’s throw-in is knocked down by Rogers into the path of Palmer who works in from the right, passing the ball around a Leeds defender and past a rooted Zetterer.

TWO goals in TWO minutes for Cole Palmer and Chelsea are level! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/sgDd3YUgA6

Chelsea 1 Leeds United 2 (Palmer) Palmer makes no mistake. He goes right, and while Zetterer guesses the right way he cannot get there and Chelsea are back in business.

Cole Palmer pulls one back for Chelsea from the spot! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/BUv6h1wTPQ

Chavarria is caught by James in the box and the referee points to the spot. That came from nowhere.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 2 (Aaronson) Amapadu deserves so much credit here. He steals the ball from Barco high, bursts beyond Rogers on the right and while Nmecha cannot turn in his cutback, Aaronson arrives late to stroke the ball past Penders and double Leeds’ lead.

"Chelsea cut apart AGAIN !" Brenden Aaronson makes it 2-0 to Leeds 🔥 pic.twitter.com/LlJNpqXHav

Alonso resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes at the interval. Palmer, Rogers, James and Neto enter the fray in place of Estevao, Watson, Gittens and Gusto.

Big cheers from the Chelsea fans at half-time, as Cole Palmer, Pedro Neto, Morgan Rogers and Reece James have all come on to warm up and are stripped off ready to play. Alonso is sending on the cavalry.

The delayed kick-off has knocked us out of kilter with tonight’s Champions League matches, but here are the live scores:

Liverpool 2 Atletico Madrid 1Paris St-Germain 4 Slovan 0Napoli 0 Arsenal 0Sporting CP 1 Galatasaray 1

Boos at half-time from the Chelsea fans. Their team were pretty awful, but booing so early in the season. Really?

There is only one minute of time added on and Watson earns himself a booking for a late challenge on Wilson before the half-time whistle is blown. It will be interesting to see how long Alonso waits before turning to his bench.

Justin, James and Wilson have got a lot of joy down Leeds’ right, rotating in Chavarria’s orbit. It has been difficult for Chelsea to pin them down and Gittens’ attacking threat has been blunted as he attempts to track their movements.

Better from Chelsea. Watson does well to regain possession high and Estevao takes over, darting towards the by-line. His cutback is directed towards Welbeck but he is beaten to the ball by a Leeds toe and it is played behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Chelsea are really struggling to build up a head of steam, with individual mistakes proving costly.

Gittens and Estevao both end up on the left and the former works infield before firing a shot at Zetterer which the German parries behind for a corner. Perhaps Chelsea’s most dangerous moment of the half.

The corner is played short with the ball eventually falling to Barco on the edge of the box but his mis-hit effort trickles wide.

Gittens rescues an overhit Acheampong cross and finds Barco on the edge of the box, but the Argentine’s effort is charged down. Leeds spring a counter and their sweeping move up field earns them a corner.

Wilson floats another delivery to the back post to Muharemovic, but he cannot replicate his earlier goal.

Farke will be delighted with what he has seen so far. It is all well and good Chelsea allowing Leeds the ball, but they have to break incisively when openings arise, and they have not done that.

Big chance for Leeds! James bursts down the right and the Welsh winger dinks in a cross to the far post which Justin cannot get past Acheampong, but while Longstaff is first to the second ball, he can only sky the shot over the bar.

Leeds’ goal has stirred something inside them and they look motivated to score a second. Ampadu launches a long throw from the left which ricochets off a couple of players before rolling out for a Chelsea goal-kick.

Chelsea 0 Leeds United 1 (Muharemovic) Set-pieces have been a massive feature of Leeds’ game this season and here they take the lead with the simplest of corner routines. Wilson floats the ball to the back post where Muharemovic is waiting, unmarked, and he loops a header over Penders into the net. Such a shame for the Chelsea keeper as he had just pulled off a stunning double-save.

"The set-piece routine does it again!" Tarik Muharemović puts Leeds in front against Chelsea! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/UxeJ3xgL56

Barco slips on the far side and in doing so concedes a corner rather comically, to the delight of the travelling supporters. The delivery is met by Lacroix and Leeds are unable to create anything from the second phase of the set-piece.

There is an intriguing duel developing down Chelsea’s right as Bard looks to contain Estevao. The French wing-back has done a decent job so far.

Estevao attempts to free himself of Bard’s clutches and drifts inside, Chavarria then almost picks him out with a cross from the left but Leeds just about clear their lines.

Justin plays in a cultured through-ball from a wide-right position to James but Chavarria does well to snuff it out. Leeds are making the pitch as big as possible and spaces are beginning to open up as they did at Fulham on the opening weekend.

Although Penders’ shot-stopping has not yet been tested, he has shown some nifty footwork, sweeping up any loose balls that make it past Chelsea’s back three/five.

Big chance! Chelsea spring a surprise attack as Chavarria sets Gittens away down the left. He works the ball infield to Welbeck who lays on a great chance for Estevao but Justin darts back to take the ball off the Brazilian’s toes. A brilliant piece of last-ditch defending.

Gittens gets a shot away, a tame effort straight at Zetterer from 22 yards out as he cuts in from the left. The correct intent, though.

Leeds look to circulate the ball across their back line. As mentioned pre-match, Chelsea will not mind letting their opponents get on the ball as they set out-of-possession traps. Aaronson eventually dribbles off the pitch on the far side.

Chelsea’s Argentine midfielder, Valentin Barco, is being booed by the Leeds fans every time he touches the ball. Barco will already be used to getting that treatment, as it has even happened to him while he’s been a substitute this season.

In other news, there’s a real Borussia Dortmund vibe to this Leeds away kit.

Leeds supporters boo Argentina World Cup squad member Barco’s every touch, and another Leeds foul, this time Justin on Gittens, prompts a second Chelsea free-kick.

A couple of early touches for Watson who plays a neat pass around the corner. Ampadu then lands a late tackle on Lacroix and Chelsea earn a free-kick in their own half.

Although there are still some empty seats, we are finally under way. Chelsea in their customary all blue, kicking from right to left. Leeds in their yellow away strip.

Chelsea and Leeds emerge from the tunnel, led out by Colwill and former Chelsea defender Ampadu. Here’s a reminder of the teams in full:

As recently as March, a giant mural of Estêvão Willian appeared on the side of a building outside Stamford Bridge as the teenager threatened to become Chelsea’s number one poster boy.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

“We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Tonight represents an opportunity for 16-year-old Reggie Watson to announce himself at senior level. Good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

If Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

#1697. How Arsenal have evolved in 2026-27

There was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title. Would lifting the Premier League trophy lead to a new era of more expressive, urbane football?

I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent. Most of Arsenal’s elite talent is behind the ball. Arteta didn’t build Arsenal from the defence first, in my view, because he felt specifically that was the best way. It was just the area of the team that required the most attention when he was appointed.

In attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced. Aubameyang, Lacazette and Pepe with Saka and Martinelli coming to the boil was a good collection of talent, even if the pieces didn’t always fit neatly together. The list of defenders he inherited included Mustafi, Sokratis, Holding, Chambers, Kolasinac and Mari. That’s why he went defence first, broadly speaking.

The moves the club have tried to make in recent seasons, especially this summer, shows you that Arteta wants his attack to be sharper than it is. For reasons I won’t relitigate here, the club were not able to add a number of high end attacking targets. Which means once again, Arsenal are reliant on Arteta’s coaching talents to squeeze more juice from the orange. Here are three things that have jumped out at me this season.

Arsenal spent a lot of money on Bruno Guimaraes this season and I will come onto some of the reasons why in the next section. But that signing has given Arteta a deep well of central options, with Rice, Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Odegaard, Merino and Zubimendi part of this midfield menagerie.

Arsenal use these options interchangeably and often according to game state. Art de Roche of the Athletic went into how Arteta has used the divergent profiles of Myles Lewis Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes so far in this campaign. In home games against Leeds and Everton, Lewis Skelly got the nod from the start.

In away games at Nottingham Forest and Liverpool, Bruno’s more robust approach was favoured. The pair have made significant impacts from the bench too. When the 1-0 victory at Anfield had become a little too ‘basketball’, Lewis Skelly came on and provided calm assurance in possession.

When the Gunners needed a little more belligerence away at Sunderland, Bruno came on and larruped the ball into the top corner from 25 yards. However, Arteta didn’t part with a significant part of his summer budget for a 28-year-old (he turns 29 next week but, for now, he remains 28 because that’s how it works) to be a high level rotation option.

Against Hull City last weekend, Bruno was selected and he played deeper than Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. As Adrian Clarke pointed out in his match analysis piece, Bruno passed the ball to Odegaard 25 times in that match and the pair exchanged 35 passes in total. The idea was clear, to use Bruno’s punchiness in possession a little lower to feed Odegaard.

Against Everton, Mikel Merino was selected in midfield and Lewis Skelly started at left-back. I think this was about more than mere rotation. Arteta always highly respects the aerial capabilities of David Moyes’ Everton team, which makes sense since he played in a David Moyes Everton team for such a long time.

In 2023-24, Arteta selected Fabio Vieira ahead of Kai Havertz in midfield at Goodison Park because he wanted to keep the ball on the floor (Arsenal won that game 1-0 via a short corner routine because they did not see the logic of aerial corners against a team like Everton).

Last season at the Hill Dickinson Arsenal enjoyed a season high for passes attempted and completed because they wanted to keep the ball on the floor and avoid transitions. Arteta has a carousel available to him in midfield and a different club in the bag depending on what is called for on the day.

Per Opta, Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times so far this season, at least 11 more times than any other team. That rate of 3.5 offsides per game is the highest of any Premier League team since 2009. Kai Havertz has been flagged 15 times now, the next highest offender in the league is Dominic Calvert-Lewin with eight. Opta provide a deeper dive on those numbers here.

So what does this tell us, aside from the fact that Havertz needs to work on his timing? It means that Arsenal are far more willing to go in behind and they are willing to test the opposition backline earlier in moves. This was a big part of the reason they signed Bruno in the first place, Arteta wants to play with the risk reward dial with the ball.

Havertz also hasn’t been quite good enough to finish some of those one v one situations when he has got in behind the opponent’s back line. He fluffed his lines against Hull last weekend and in the 3-0 defeat at Brighton, he blasted his effort straight at the Brighton keeper when put through one v one.

But here, I will express my usual caveat, we need to normalise strikers missing chances and focus more on process than outcome. Most chances are missed, you want to worry when your striker is getting few shots. There have also been nascent signs that Arsenal have been using Gyokeres well in some of these situations.

That Havertz chance at the Amex was created by Gyokeres taking one touch with his back to goal and hooking the ball past the committed defensive line. Gyokeres did much the same for Madueke in Prague. It seems like Arsenal have worked on getting Gyokeres to use his physicality to initially retain the ball- something he badly struggled with last season- but creating situations where he can release it quickly.

Arsenal’s out of possession prowess is one thing that has been a constant from last season. It is Arsenal’s superpower, so even when they can only manage one goal, it is usually enough to take maximum points. To retain their superpower, Arsenal changed to stay the same, if that makes sense.

The signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa was questioned by many but his presence has made the absence of a world class centre-back like William Saliba a sidebar, which is quite a feat. Arsenal ostensibly took William Saliba’s pizza chart and looked for the most Saliba like defender they could find and bought Konsa.

The loss of Saliba ought to have offered an enormous threat to Arsenal’s defensive stability. Arsenal’s tactical organisation out of possession is elite but so too are the individuals that helm it. Raya, Saliba, Gabriel and Rice are among the best players in the world in their respective positions.

Taking out one of those pillars ought to have derailed Arsenal’s defensive stability and it hasn’t because Konsa has the quality and poise to retain the team’s biggest strength. His pass completion stats are Saliba-esque and the quality of not giving the ball away needlessly is a significant part of the Gunners’ meanness.

How much Arsenal could improve in attack without significant additions was an unknown so Arteta could not afford to sacrifice the team’s defensive ceiling while he plays with those levers. The addition of Konsa was a personnel change that allowed Arsenal to remain the same.

#1696. Moretto: Tresoldi ‘arrived at Casa Milan’ to sign but move collapsed – the background

Nicolo Tresoldi could have already been an AC Milan player now, given that he was very close to signing a few years ago.

Tresoldi has found himself in the Milan orbit for a number of reasons in recent weeks. His continued declarations of love for the Rossoneri – his boyhood team – already had some fans clamouring to try and sign him, and that was before his Champions League hat-trick against Inter at San Siro.

In the past few days, the speculation has ramped up regarding an attempt by Milan. Not put off by the painful negotiations to sign Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari, it seems Gerry Cardinale wants to try and sign yet another Brugge star.

Matteo Moretto spoke during a video on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, and he explained that the young striker was even close to signing for Milan previously, while waiting to see what the future holds.

“In the summer of 2021, Tresoldi arrived at Casa Milan because he had every intention of signing for Milan. Milan had already closed on him,” he said (via MilanNews).

“At the time, the Maldini-Massara duo were the ones at the helm. The deal was done, all that was missing was the signatures. Tresoldi didn’t sign that day: he returned to Germany, and Milan never closed the deal.

“In the summer of 2021, Milan came close to signing Tresoldi, but he then extended his contract with Hannover. We’ll see if he can become a popular option for the Rossoneri in the future.”

#1694. Manchester United face £900m Adidas deal threat amid relegation fears

By Naim Beneddra | 11 Nov 2026 17:14

Manchester United's worsening Premier League campaign could have significant financial consequences, with a relegation clause in their £900m Adidas contract allowing the sportswear manufacturer to halve its annual payments to the club.

Michael Carrick's side have entered the November international break in the relegation zone, sitting 18th with just eight points from their opening 10 league matches.

United have won only once in the Premier League this season and are without a victory in their last eight top-flight fixtures, equalling their longest winless run in the competition's history.

Sunday's extraordinary 4-4 draw with Aston Villa offered some relief after two stoppage-time goals rescued a point at Old Trafford, but the result did little to improve their precarious league position.

Their struggles have brought renewed attention to the commercial implications of a potential drop into the Championship, with the club's latest financial disclosures confirming a provision that could substantially reduce one of their most lucrative revenue streams.

Although relegation remains a hypothetical outcome with much of the season still to play, United's Adidas agreement includes both a payment reduction mechanism and a potential termination clause.

United agreed a 10-year extension to their partnership with Adidas in July 2023, taking their relationship with the German sportswear company through to June 2035.

The extension carries a minimum guarantee of £900m, in addition to the £750m guaranteed under the original agreement, bringing the total contractual guarantee across the extended partnership to £1.65bn, subject to adjustments.

However, the club's annual report for the financial year ending June 30, 2026 confirms that those payments are not entirely protected against a decline in sporting fortunes.

Under the agreement, Adidas has the right to reduce the applicable payments for any year by 50% if United's men's first team are not competing in the Premier League.

Crucially, that would be a reduction in the relevant annual payment, rather than an automatic loss of £900m.

The agreement also gives Adidas the option of terminating its partnership by providing one full season's notice if United are relegated from the Premier League or are otherwise excluded from England's top division.

That provision does not mean a termination would automatically follow relegation, but it would give the manufacturer a contractual route to end the relationship.

United's financial disclosures also confirm a separate penalty for failing to qualify for the Champions League.

From the 2025-26 season onwards, their agreement includes a £10m deduction for each campaign in which the men's team do not participate in Europe's premier club competition.

The club's failure to qualify for the 2025-26 Champions League already triggered one such deduction.

These clauses illustrate how United's commercial income is linked to their performances on the pitch, even under a long-term agreement with one of the world's biggest sportswear brands.

The relegation provision would only become relevant if the club actually dropped out of the Premier League, but their current position has made a previously remote contractual scenario worthy of attention.

United have not played outside England's top flight since the 1974-75 campaign, when they immediately secured promotion from the Second Division.

Their last relegation came in 1974, six years after winning the European Cup under Sir Matt Busby.

They have never been relegated during the Premier League era, which began in 1992, although their 15th-place finish in 2024-25 represented their worst final position since the competition's formation.

The current campaign has produced an even more alarming start.

United's position after 10 matches is their lowest at this stage of a top-flight season since 1986-87, when Ron Atkinson was replaced by Sir Alex Ferguson in November 1986.

Ferguson eventually guided United to an 11th-place finish that season, before overseeing a transformation that delivered 13 Premier League titles.

Carrick now faces a very different challenge, with his side having conceded 19 league goals and secured only one win from their first 10 fixtures.

The latest setback came against Aston Villa, when United recovered from two goals down on two separate occasions before Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu scored in stoppage time.

Their resilience earned a point, but defensive mistakes continued to undermine the team.

Carrick acknowledged afterwards that United had been making matches unnecessarily difficult through avoidable errors, while insisting that their overall performance deserved more than a draw.

The Red Devils will return from the international break with a trip to Liverpool on November 22, a fixture that presents another difficult test of their attempts to climb away from the bottom three.

For now, there is no suggestion that Adidas has taken action over United's league position. The contractual consequences would depend on their final status at the end of the season.

Nevertheless, the club's financial filings establish precisely what could be at stake should their worst start in four decades eventually result in an unprecedented Premier League relegation.

#1693. Salamanca CF UDS vs Celta Vigo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 17:22, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 17:30

Celta Vigo will aim to avoid a shock elimination in the first round of the Copa del Rey when they tackle fourth-tier outfit Salamanca CF UDS on Friday night.

The visitors have been runners-up in the Copa del Rey on three previous occasions, including in 2000-01, while Salamanca have never been past the second round of the tournament.

Salamanca are managed by a legendary figure in La Liga, with ex-Athletic Bilbao forward Iker Muniain at the helm of the Spanish outfit.

Muniain played 560 matches for Athletic during his professional career, and he is now tasked with helping Salamanca provide a shock in the first round of the 2026-27 Copa del Rey.

Salamanca have been a fourth-tier outfit since 2024-25, earning promotion from the fifth tier in 2023-24, and they are aiming to reach the second round of the Copa del Rey for just the second time in their history, previously securing a spot at that stage in 2024-25.

The hosts will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 win over Real Avila in the league, and they also recorded a 1-0 victory in their last home fixture over Gimnastia Segoviana on November 1.

This fixture had originally been due to take place at the end of October, but it was postponed following the tragic train crash in the province of Toledo, and it was then agreed by both clubs to be played during the international break.

Celta will enter this match off the back of a goalless draw with Levante; the result left them 11th in the La Liga table, picking up 13 points from 12 matches.

The Sky Blues are also playing in the Europa League this season, picking up three points from their four matches in the competition to sit 27th in the overall table.

Claudio Giraldez's side will resume their La Liga action against Real Madrid on November 21 but first have to navigate their way into the second round of the Copa del Rey.

Celta have never won the Copa del Rey, but they have reached the final of the tournament on three previous occasions, lastly finishing as runners-up in 2000-01, suffering a 3-1 defeat to Real Zaragoza in Seville.

The Sky Blues have previously faced Salamanca in the Copa del Rey, recording a 7-0 victory when the two teams locked horns in December 2024.

Salamanca CF UDS form (all competitions):

Salamanca are expected to have Larry Opara at the tip of their attack on Friday, while William Pena is expected to feature in a wide area for the hosts.

Oscar Leon has scored twice in 10 appearances for Salamanca this season, and the 21-year-old is also in line to feature in the starting team.

Salamanca have not reported any injury problems for this match, so head coach Muniain could have a full squad available for the standout Copa del Rey fixture.

Celta have been boosted by the news that Ilaix Moriba has withdrawn from the Guinea squad and will therefore be available for the clash with Salamanca.

However, Sebastian Caceres is unavailable due to international commitments with Uruguay.

Celta will also be missing Borja Iglesias, Carl Starfelt, Jones El Abdellaoui, Alvaro Nunez and Miguel Roman for the cup fixture due to injury problems.

Celta are set to name a strong side on Friday, and we are expecting the Sky Blues to comfortably secure their spot in the next round of the competition.

#1691. Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!

Published: 16:25 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 16:27 EST, 7 November 2026

'Peak FA Cup', was the verdict from TV viewers watching (or trying to watch) the clash between Notts County and Altrincham as thick fog obscured the action.

Those tuning in on TNT Sports were baffled by what was actually happening in the game when the mist descended at Moss Lane.

Commentators saw the funny side, with Adam Summerton chuckling, saying: 'Your guess is as good as mine at the minute,' when asked by his partner what was going on.

As the match progressed, the foggy conditions only worsened and it became difficult for the players to see far in front of them, let alone those trying to spectate in the ground and at home.

Even though the conditions appeared to simply be deep fog, one local claimed it was smoke from local firework parties causing the white-out.

They wrote: 'It is smoke from the bonfire night fireworks and bonfires. I live round the corner, it is literally just smoke. All you can smell in the air is smoke.'

The fog is closing in at Moss Lane! 🌫️Conditions are getting tricky for Altrincham and Notts County 👀📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/gTM9e3KA2w

Fog descended on the FA Cup clash between Altrincham and Notts County and TV viewers could hardly tell what was going on

Fans pulled out the torches on their phones in a light-hearted bid to see more of the action

Despite the lack of quality action for fans to watch at Moss Lane, plenty of them saw the funny side and even took out their phone torches in unison to try and cut through the gloom.

Those at home poked fun at the scene, with one posting: 'Can you ask the ref that if it goes to pens they bring the goal closer to the cameras so we can watch them?'

Another wrote: 'Where's the orange ball? I miss those days!'

Not everyone could see the humour in the situation, with one user on X writing: 'I'm sorry but this is ridiculous it should be abandoned. You could be miles offside.'

The game itself went to penalties, which caused further problems for the commentators, who had to largely base their reactions on the crowd directly behind the goal.

Ultimately, Notts County survived a scare from the non-league outfit and won 3-2 in the shootout.

Rosaire Longelo netted the final spot-kick to fire the Magpies into the second round of the FA Cup.

They'd had to fight back from 2-1 down in normal time after Lucas Weaver and then Lewis Banks put Altrincham in front.

Callum Roberts scored to make it 2-2 and neither side could find a winner in extra-time, meaning an already memorable game was settled in a fitting and dramatic fashion.

#1690. Chelsea injury news: Blues handed Josh Acheampong blow

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 17:38

Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong has allegedly withdrawn from international duty with England Under-21s.

Having been largely snubbed by the likes of Enzo Maresca and Liam Rosenior, the 20-year-old has starred under Xabi Alonso.

In sharp contrast to 2025-26, Acheampong has accumulated the sixth most minutes of Chelsea's outfield players in this season's Premier League.

However, the academy graduate was a notable absentee from the squad that suffered a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland last weekend.

At the time, the injury being carried by the versatile defender was described as 'minor'.

According to football.london journalist Bobby Vincent, Acheampong has now withdrawn from representing England Under-21s over the November international break.

When Acheampong remained in the group at the start of the week, the assumption had been that he would be available for the games against Portugal and France.

Instead, the youngster has seemingly returned to Chelsea, where he will be assessed ahead of the resumption of Premier League action later in the month.

The report emphasises that Acheampong's fitness issue is not expected to keep him out in the long term.

Presumably, playing him in two international friendlies has not been deemed worth the risk.

He has already racked up nine starts and two substitute outings for Chelsea this season, as well as made two starts for England Under-21s.

Therefore, a brief rest before the resumption of action may prove to be a blessing in disguise for a player who barely played between January and June.

#1689. Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

“It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick said. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

Mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick said. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick said. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

“Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”

81 - Kobbie Mainoo completed the most passes in Manchester United's 4-0 win over Sabah (81).It was the most by an Englishman for the Red Devils in a UEFA Champions League match since Michael Carrick in February 2014 vs Olympiakos (89).Mentor. pic.twitter.com/59wSvQydOG

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

Dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Fenerbahce 1 Roma 1 FTPSV 1 Shakhtar Donetsk 1 (FTBayern Munich 0 Bodo/Glimt 0 HTComo 2 RB Leipzig 0 HTManchester United 3 Sabah 0 HTSlavia Prague 0 Lens 0 HT

Those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Possession: Manchester United 59%-41% SabahShots: 14-4Shots on target: 5-0Corners: 6-2Touches in opposition box: 35-4

The first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

That is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM

Michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

That’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The Brazilian has his first Champions League goal but it is gifted by Sabah. The visitors are threatening a counter-attack but Parris inexplicably gives the ball away on halfway with a dreadful pass across the pitch. The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. A sense of frustration had been growing inside Old Trafford but Sabah have rather gifted Manchester United the opener there.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq

Sabah give it away inside their own half and Manchester United flood forward towards the Sabah penalty area. Mbuemo drives forward and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before getting his shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at Pokatilov.

That is outstanding defensive work from Dasdamirov. Mainoo plays a quite sensational first-time ball in behind into the right channel to pick out the run of Fernandez. The Manchester United captain has Sesko waiting in the middle for the cross but Dasdamirov steps in with an absolutely essential interception or else Sesko would have had a tap-in.

Sabah need to be careful as now a few times they have been caught in possession deep in their own territory.

Cunha sends in a corner from the left that threatens to go in at the far corner but Sabah keeper Pokatilov catches it near his own line.

Sabah are making their Champions League debut and so too tonight are Cesc Fabregas’ Como, who have just taken the lead at home against RB Leipzig. Manchester United will travel to Como in late October on matchday three. Manchester United play RB Leipzig at home on matchday six.

Sabah have to negotiate a couple of Manchester United corners in quick succession and they do so. The visitors’ starting XI tonight has a very international feel to it:

Sabah FC have named a starting XI featuring 11 different nationalities 🌍🇰🇿 Stas Pokatilov🇩🇿 Akim Zedadka🇦🇿 Rahman Dashdamirov🇿🇦 Aden McCarthy🇵🇱 Tymoteusz Puchacz🇺🇿 Umarali Rakhmonaliev🇭🇷 Ivan Lepinjica🇯🇲 Kaheem Parris🇷🇸 Veljko Simic🇳🇬 Christian Nwachukwu🇷🇼 Joy-Lance… pic.twitter.com/ih5Sf1aeie

Mazraoui, despite starting at right-back, has already had three shots in the game. Two have been outside the box that have been blocked and the latest hits the side netting from the right side of the penalty area.

Mazraoui plays a pass forward into Cunha on the right side of the box and the Brazilian tries to beat Pokatilov at the near post but the Sabah keeper makes the save and pushes it around the post for a corner.

Sabah are able to clear their lines from Mbeumo’s delivery.

Sabah seem content to take risks on the ball deep inside their own half and play out from the back. Will that be a masterstroke or is it asking for trouble?

Sabah make their first foray into the Manchester United penalty area and there are appeals for handball. It did hit Dorgu’s hand but it was right down by his side and that is not a deliberate handball. Sabah do win a corner, which Dorgu heads away.

Sesko, fresh off what he thought was going to be the winner at Everton on Sunday, has been given the nod to start up top for the home side tonight. He is very close to closing the Sabah goalkeeper Pokatilov down inside his own six-yard box and that was nearly a horrific moment for the Champions League debutants a matter of minutes into their debut in this competition.

Sabah started their journey through the qualifying rounds of this comeptition back in the early parts of July so they have already played quite a number of games so far this season, in comparison to Manchester United’s three competitive fixtures coming into tonight.

As has been the case at every Champions League game this week, there is a moment silence to remember the victims of the recent deadly floods in Nepal.

We are under way at Old Trafford. Manchester United, three-time winners of this trophy, return to the Champions League whilst Sabah make their debut in the competition.

It’s 1,003 days since the Champions League anthem has been heard at Old Trafford and, to be honest, it feels longer. There are about 500 Sabah fans here tonight.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Old Trafford and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Manchester United: Lammens, Mazraoui, Yoro, Martinez, Dorgu, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha, Sesko.Substitutes: Darlow, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Heaven, Maguire, Santos, Mount, T. Fletcher, Lacey, Rashford, Zirkzee.

Sabah: Pokatilov, McCarthy, Dashdamirov, Rakhmonaliev, Nwachukwu, Parris, Lepinjica, Mickels, Simic, Puchacz, Zedadka.Substitutes: Ramazanov, Mirzammadov, Khaibulaev, Isaev, Rustamli, Mutallimov, Almeida, Quiroz, Fernandes, Mukhtarov, Mbina.

Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench.
