And now sent off after 24 minutes.

A half that will be remembered for one thing and one thing only: Phil Foden’s red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

United were shading things before that flashpoint, but City will be pleased with their response to the sending off. They have defended well, and posed a threat going forward without executing the final pass or shot.

This is now a different game to the one United were expecting, so perhaps Carrick needs to shuffle the pack.

United win a free-kick about 25 yards from goal after Enzo Fernandez chases his own poor touch and fouls Tielemans.

Rashford to take... cracking hit, up and over the wall but the attempt bounces wide off the post.

United struggling to carve out clear openings, nobody was planning for the game to have this pattern with the home team dominating possession and City dropping off into a deep defensive shape. Nunes does exceptionally well to win a tackle, drive out from the back and find Cherki.

City threaten again after a poor defensive header by Dalot, with Semenyo fizzing in a low cross that is deflected behind for a corner with Fernandez lurking in the six-yard box. United have lost their way in the last 10 minutes, Dalot flagged offside unnecessarily.

There’s a reminder of City’s threat: Haaland spinning a pass wide right to Cherki who is in acres, but with Haaland in the middle and Semenyo on the edge of the box he crosses to nobody at the back stick.

He was not a starter in Carrick’s original game plan, but I wonder if United’s task now calls for Benjamin Sesko and some extra penalty-box presence and aerial threat. Guehi is having a very sound game at the back for City.

Both teams adjusting after the red card, Cherki and Semenyo are trying to put in a defensive shift in front of their full-backs. United enjoying the majority of possession, and Fernandes feeds Rashford with a delightful reverse pass but Rashford’s first touch was loose.

United will now be favourites to win this game, but Mainoo was required to block a goal-bound strike from Cherki after a corner was clear. City do have the ammunition to offer a threat on the break. They need the Haaland of his Dortmund days to attack big spaces on the counter.

Old Trafford is delirious because United’s scourge in so many derbies is off for an early shower. England manager Thomas Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry are among those in attendance at Old Trafford ahead of Friday’s squad announcement, the first since the World Cup and ahead of the forthcoming Nations League campaign. There are plenty of players on show, on both sides ,who will hope to be in contention including Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford for United although Harry Maguire may have talked his way out of being considered after his reaction to not making the World Cup squad. Very wasteful from Haaland, after Bruno Fernandes’s stray wall pass back into midfield ran into his path. Neither picked a pass nor let fly with a shot and lost control of the ball.

At the other end, Guehi defends well against Rashford and City have a goal kick, but United have the upper hand in the game at the moment.

Cunha with a burst through City’s midfield and he is brought down by Fernandez. City with a more sustained spell of possession in the United half, but Martinez defends well as Foden dribbles into the penalty area. Cunha then tries to release Rashford behind the City defence, but Dias covered well behind Guehi to intercept.

Then Fernandes’s next pass is more threatening, lofting a pass over the City defence for the run of Diogo Dalot but he cannot quite put the ball under his spell in the penalty area.

Rashford finds himself near the right touchline and finds room to drive inside with the ball, where he is sandwiched between Semenyo and Anderson. Free-kick for United in a crossing position right of centre, and from the second phase a Martinez cross flies into the gloves of Donnarumma.

An early glimpse of United’s slightly flimsy central midfield with Cherki finding space behind them and Enzo Fernandez’s strike from distance deflecting over the bar. Martinez heads Anderson’s delivery behind for another corner.

This time City take it short, but United clear their lines when the ball is crossed into the box.

The ball changes hands in midfield a couple of times in quick succession. Dalot pressing Semenyo but the winger gets away from him, but United win a challenge before Anderson nips in. Promising start if you want aggression and intensity.

Maguire is then penalised for a foul on Cherki in a more promising position for City, but from a free-kick taken short the flag goes up for offside. City claim there was a foul on Cherki from Fernandes.

United get the first Manchester derby of the season under way.

As expected, there is that banner above the mouth of the tunnel.

“THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE” banner is displayed above the Munich tunnel on the south west corner of the Stretford End.

We’ve got a lot of encouragement going into the season, of course we wanted more points at this stage. Michael Carrick’s record has been outstanding, particularly at Old Trafford. They’ve been brilliant here and very difficult to beat.

Inside Old Trafford, all flags in the Stretford End are set to be removed with and replaced by one banner that reads: “THE WAY YOU TREAT US IS A DISGRACE.”

Struck by the nature of both midfields. The other five are not especially adept at covering ground and defensive actions, so this could well be wide open.

Thousands of Manchester United fans have been marching in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s running of the club.

Supporters have reacted with outrage to the club’s handling of a controversial anti ticket touting operation they felt unfairly singled out innocent fans.

And thousands have taken to the streets to voice their anger at how they feel they are being treated by the co-owners.

Plumes of red and green and yellow smoke filled the air as fans brandished banners and flags and chanted anti-Glazer and Ratcliffe songs.

“You take it all from fans and banning us for nothing. Premium prices all for greed,” read one banner.

One banner is a Stones Roses-themed number emblazoned with “Jim Aint The One”, a nod to Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the song This Is The One which is played at Old Trafford as the teams emerge from the tunnel.

Enzo Maresca has selected the more attacking option by playing Enzo Fernandez deeper alongside Elliot Anderson, rather than pushing the Argentine up a line and starting O’Reilly or Bouaddi. Still no Doku for City, and Foden has been preferred to Ndiaye out wide.

Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu, Tielemans, Mainoo, Mbeumo, Cunha, Fernandes, Rashford

Subs: Darlow, Heaven, Mazraoui, Yoro, Mount, Santos, Lacey, Sesko, Zirkzee.

Representing the Reds on derby day... 📋❤️‍🔥COME ON UNITED! 🗣️🗣️🗣️

They are now 2-0 down against Brighton and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off for an elbow. Bar a miracle, it will be zero points from four games for Frank Lampard’s team.

There will be no flags in the Stretford End today in a protest against ticketing policy which United say is about stopping touts, but loyal, innocent fans may have been caught in the crossfire. A crackdown has led to 685 supporters being stripped of their season tickets and another 464 being sanctioned. Fans will unfurl a giant banner reading “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace” aimed at the club’s hierarchy this afternoon. You can read more here from James Ducker.

"You can shove your new ground up your a*rse"#MUFC protests pic.twitter.com/EMmnF8FhNo

Kostoulas has given Brighton the lead away at Coventry, who are still to pick up their first Premier League point. Around five minutes until half-time in that one. It was quite some finish.

"What an outstanding finish, absolutely brilliant!"Charalampos Kostoulas fires Brighton in front with a wonderful finish 💥 pic.twitter.com/bMKJACr2bd

Both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

To most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very important in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

It has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

#1641. Colombia vs Chile - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 11 Nov 2026 23:58

For the first time since a devastating earthquake claimed more than 300 lives and left parts of Cali in ruins, Colombia will play on home soil when they take on Chile.

With more than 30,000 fans expected to pack the Pascual Guerrero Stadium, it promises to be an emotional occasion for the hosts as they prepare to face La Roja in the first of two international friendly encounters.

Before last summer’s tragedy, Colombia enjoyed a respectable run at the World Cup, reaching the round-of-16 where they eventually lost to Switzerland on penalties.

Prior to that disappointment, head coach Nestor Lorenzo watched his side record victories over Uzbekistan, DR Congo and Ghana, while also holding Portugal to a goalless draw during the group stage.

Since the end of the tournament, Colombia have played three international friendlies, all of which were hosted by the United States.

This means that Friday's match against Chile will mark Colombia's first return to home soil since the tragedy, with more than 4,000 travelling supporters also expected to visit Cali and provide a welcome boost to the local economy.

From a footballing perspective, the fixture offers Lorenzo an opportunity to begin laying the foundations for the next major tournament on the calendar, the 2028 Copa America.

Colombia will be eager to go one step further in the next edition after reaching the final of the previous tournament, where they suffered a narrow defeat to Lionel Messi's Argentina.

Chile will head into Friday's encounter with Nicolas Cordova reportedly approaching his final international break as interim head coach, leaving the 47-year-old keen to sign off his spell with a positive result.

During the previous international break, La Roja completed a tour of North America, where they lost against Canada and the United States before beating Mexico 2-0.

Putting those results aside, midfielder Cesar Perez has recently given Cordova public backing, arguing that the team are beginning to find their identity under his leadership.

The interim boss has largely focused on introducing the next generation of Chilean talent during his time at the helm, leaving former stalwarts Alexis Sanchez, Arturo Vidal and Eduardo Vargas out of his plans.

Looking ahead to Friday's fixture, La Roja will be hoping to end a seven-year wait for a victory over Colombia.

The two nations last met in October 2024, when Colombia cruised to a convincing 4-0 victory in their World Cup qualifying encounter.

Colombia’s head coach Lorenzo decided to call up several debutants, including Juan David Arizala, Devis Vasquez, Camilo Mena and Daniel Mosquera.

Some of those names could get minutes given the hosts are missing Richard Rios and Luis Diaz through injuries.

Jaminton Campaz has also withdrawn from the squad last Sunday after suffering muscle discomfort while playing for Rosario Central. Oscar Cortes, who is a regular starter for Argentinian side Huracan, was called up in his place.

Chile, on the other hand, are without Benjamin Kuscevic, who is out with a sprained right ankle,

There is also uncertainty surrounding Paulo Diaz, who picked up an injury in Tuesday's training session.

Chile's 26-man squad is also missing such names as Marcelino Nunez, Matias Sepulveda, and Marcelo Morales, while Guillermo Maripan is back after being left out of previous squads.

Vargas; Munoz, Sanchez, Lucumi, Velasquez; Puerta, Lerma; Asprilla, Arias, Perea; Suarez

Vigouroux; Suazo, Villagra, Roman, Ulloa; Pizarro, Loyola, Osorio; Tapia, Gutierrez, Diaz

This is no ordinary international friendly given the tragic circumstances, and Colombia will be desperate to lift the nation with a positive result on their homecoming.

Chile showed signs of improvement during their tour of North America in September, but their lack of quality could cost them here.

#1640. Report: One of the world's best has chosen Liverpool, Reds can agree deal when they want

Liverpool are the chosen club of one of the world's best. They can strike a deal whenever they want.

Liverpool have made it their mission in recent transfer windows to sign the biggest talents they can. Sometimes that's a player at the top of his game right now, other times is youth products who look destined for the very top.

Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola are perfect examples of the former. They've all performed to elite levels in top European leagues and that meant Liverpool were willing to spend an awful lot on them.

Then there are players like Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni. Stars who were destined to kick on to the elite bracket with the right development.

But there is, of course, a third way to secure elite talent.

The third way to guarantee elite talent is at your club is to lock down those you already have. And Liverpool have a couple of enormous decisions to make in that regard over the next few months.

Alisson Becker is one of those, with his contract set to expire at the end of the season. The goalkeeper, who is still performing at a truly world-class level, has voiced his preference to remain at Anfield.

And ESPN has given some details on that. They claim that there aren't currently any real negotiations between Alisson and Liverpool. Instead, both parties are happy to wait for the end of the season before committing to anything.

But Alisson has given his preference to Liverpool. That's where he wants to be and there's a sense that Liverpool could get the deal agreed whenever they want. They just prefer to wait.

We imagine that's because of Alisson's injury record. Another long-term, major injury likely ends all chance of a new deal or at least significantly weakens the goalkeeper's negotiating position.

And so if Liverpool know he wants to remain, they might as well hold off. There appears to be little fear that he'll agree terms with a different club from January 1st, certainly.

#1639. GdS: Milan open to Camarda loan to aid development – move abroad also possible

AC Milan’s plan to strengthen the attack in January could have a knock-on impact on Francesco Camarda’s fate, a report claims.

This morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport makes the bold claim that Milan are readying a winter attempt for Nicolo Tresoldi of Club Brugge. His price tag is already €50m, but the idea is to invest in the young striker and potentially pair him with Goncalo Ramos.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tresoldi’s fate intersects with that of Camarda. The Milan academy graduate has barely exceeded 100 minutes of playing time this season, 119 to be precise: 83 in the Europa League, with a single start against Salzburg, and another 36 in Serie A.

He hasn’t scored and had only one real chance to score, against Bologna. He needs to play to showcase his qualities, so the club believe it’s best to try do this elsewhere, before returning fit and ready to play for the Rossoneri.

The new development is that Camarda could develop at another Serie A team, or potentially return further enriched by experience abroad. There’s no shortage of options outside of Italy, but it will be a dry loan with no option to make it permanent.

Having arrived as a child in the Milan youth academy, he won an U15 Scudetto. He also achieved a historic record: with a federal exemption required because he was still a teenager, Camarda made his Serie A debut for AC Milan on 25 November 2023, late in the match against Fiorentina.

On that occasion, he became the youngest debutant in Serie A history (15 years, 8 months, and 15 days) and the youngest debutant in Milan’s history, surpassing the previous record set by Paolo Maldini, who made his debut at 16 years, 6 months, and 25 days.

In 2024, he signed his first professional contract and began his experience with Milan Futuro, the club’s second team, created specifically to nurture Milan’s talents, without necessarily having the need to send them elsewhere to develop.

That same season, at 16 years and 226 days, he became the youngest Italian player ever to make his Champions League debut. In 2025-26, it was time to try Serie A, where he could consistently play: he moved to Lecce, where, in 23 appearances, he scored his first (and so far only) league goal.

He was bought by the Giallorossi, and then bought back by Milan (who reserved a buy-back clause), with a contract extended until the summer of 2031 in the summer, plus an option for another year.

After progressing through Italy’s youth teams, Camarda truly found his calling with the U21s, scoring four goals in six games. He was also called up to the senior national team, playing for Baldini’s ‘experimental’ squad, making two appearances.

#1638. Dejected Dimitar Berbatov has his head in his hands as he realises Man United are now in relegation zone - but admits old side DESERVE to be there

Published: 18:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 20:33 EST, 7 November 2026

Former Manchester United legend Dimitar Berbatov has blasted his old side, saying they deserve to be in the relegation zone.

United plunged into the bottom three on Saturday afternoon, perversely as neighbours Manchester City lost 3-1 away to Nottingham Forest.

The Bulgarian looked devastated when he was informed of United’s predicament while working on beIN Sports' coverage of the City game but still sounded hopeful that United could turn their form around.

When his attention was drawn to the Premier League table, the two-time Premier League winner initially had his head in his hands before saying: 'I don't believe it, but the way United are playing sometimes they deserve to be there honestly.'

Berbatov then took up a more positive tune saying: ‘Tomorrow they still have a game.'

United host Aston Villa on Sunday and after winning against Roma in midweek have the perfect opportunity finally to end their seven-game winless run in the league.

Berbatov could barely look at the table after United plunged into the drop zone

Berbatov won five major trophies as well as Premier League golden boot in four years at Manhchetser United

The fixture could prove either to be the nail in the coffin for United manager Michael Carrick or afford him more time after a woeful start to the season.

Berbatov won his two Premier Leagues alongside Carrick and will hope his ex-colleague can find a way to keep his job.

If he fails to guide his team to a victory against Villa it could be bleak for Carrick, as he has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa.

Club chiefs handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in ten games.

But now the onus is on Carrick to build on the momentum gained from their Champions League victory.

#1637. Report: Julian Ward has made his mind up on 'outstanding' Liverpool star's future

Julian Ward has a lot of issues to solve ahead of his first transfer window as Liverpool's new sporting director.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes at the end of the 2026-27 summer window and was given a tough act to follow.

During his time as Liverpool's sporting director, Hughes spent well over £600 million on new players and, even though most fans thought that they'd be sorted for the next few years, there are still some major red flags among their ranks.

And, the fact that some star players such as Ronald Araujo don't have their futures ironed out yet is massively concerning.

However, as with every job, tough decisions need to be made and now, it seems like the Reds have come to a decision on one star.

Liverpool will not sell Jeremie Frimpong in January

Recently, a lot of talk has occurred about the future of some Liverpool players.

At the moment, the Reds are massively underperforming and find themselves fourth in the Premier League table.

The fact that they're already nine points adrift of first-place Arsenal after just 10 games is quite scary.

However, with the January window coming up soon, their fortunes could be about to change.

Many different rumours have emerged from L4 recently with some even linking Jeremie Frimpong with a move to Al-Hilal.

But, after this latest update from Football Insider, that doesn't seem to be the case.

"The Reds have no intention of cashing in on the Dutchman this winter, and are wary about potentially leaving their squad short of depth for the rest of the campaign," they wrote.

"However, sources say that if a 'big offer' were to arrive from Saudi Arabia in the summer, then it is something that both Frimpong and the club would be open to.

"Liverpool have enjoyed a bright start to the season under Iraola, but are wary that their situation in defence is a little precarious at the moment.

"The boss does not have the level of squad depth that he would like, and feels that his group is lighter than several direct rivals.

"With that in mind, the club believe that they cannot afford to let Frimpong go in January, regardless of the interest from Al-Hilal."

Jeremie Frimpong still has an important role to play at Liverpool

It's not a surprise to anyone to find out that Frimpong hasn't performed very well since he joined Liverpool last season.

The right-back was brought in to become Trent Alexander-Arnold's replacement with his goal and assist record at Bayer Leverkusen rather extraordinary.

But, for one reason or another, things just haven't clicked for the Dutchman at Anfield.

And, while Araujo may have made the right-back spot his own this season, there is still the odd game here and there where Frimpong is needed.

His pace, coupled with his attacking prowess are two pieces of skill that Liverpool are lacking in at the moment.

So, even if Al-Hilal do actually want to sign the 25-year-old at some point in the future, right now, he's too valuable for Liverpool to get rid of.

Here's hoping that, even if the "outstanding" defender does leave next summer, he manages to find some sort of form before the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

#1636. Qatar vs Australia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 11 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 00:07

In the first of two friendlies each in the November international break, Qatar and Australia will meet in Doha on Friday.

The visitors met Brazil twice in the September break after their World Cup exit in the summer, while their hosts last competed in the Arabian Gulf Cup after their own World Cup campaign.

Qatar head into their first game of the international break on Friday aiming to get back to winning ways after a busy spell since the summer.

They spent June in the USA and Canada for the 2026 World Cup, their second consecutive appearance and first in their history away from home soil, but failed to qualify from the group stage having only drawn against Switzerland and lost to Canada and Bosnia and Herzegovina, conceding 10 goals in those three matches.

Focus then turned to the Arabian Gulf Cup across September and October, and Julen Lopetegui's side qualified for the semi-finals by earning seven points from three group games, beating Bahrain and Yemen 2-0 and 1-0 respectively and drawing against United Arab Emirates.

Saudi Arabia stood between them and the final, and the Maroons fell just short in Jeddah, losing in a penalty shootout after a goalless stalemate across 120 minutes.

Now heading into their first friendlies since the World Cup preparation, with their next competitive action not until December 2027, Qatar have a chance to regroup and will hope to put an impressive win on the board on home soil on Friday.

Their opponents, meanwhile, faced a difficult double-header in the previous international break and will now go in search of two victories in a trip to the Middle East.

Australia also spent their summer at the World Cup and did enough to qualify for the knockout stage for the second straight edition with four points in the group, beating Turkey 2-0, losing by the same scoreline to USA and drawing against Paraguay.

Tony Popovic's team would bow out in the round of 32, though, drawing against Egypt thanks to an own goal and losing in the penalty shootout, before they hosted Brazil in September for a pair of friendlies.

Against a strong Selecao side, the Socceroos were able to draw the first game 1-1, albeit with Rayan drawing the visitors level in injury time after Nestory Irankunda's opener, before they lost the second meeting 4-2 having led 2-1 in the first half through Alessandro Circati and Connor Metcalfe.

Now also not in competitive action until the Asian Cup late next year, Australia will look to record a pair of victories in their final international games of 2026.

Qatar have called up a similar squad from the Gulf Cup, with the only notable absence from that group being goalkeeper Meshaal Barsham.

There is plenty of experience throughout, with Hassan Al-Haydos, Akram Afif, Boualem Khoukhi, Karim Boudiaf, Almoez Ali and Pedro Miguel all boasting more than 110 caps.

Ali should continue to spearhead the attack with 61 goals to his name in 132 appearances for his nation, while captain Al-Haydos could return to the attack from the start as he nears the 200-cap mark.

Australia have also called up a strong squad for their friendlies, with midfielders Jackson Irvine and Aiden O'Neill among the only notable absentees from their squad against Brazil while Alex Robertson also missed out on a call-up.

Patrick Beach will continue in net as the long-term heir to Mathew Ryan, while Alessandro Circati and Hull City's Lucas Herrington may again join mainstay Harry Souttar in defence.

Kusini Yengi should continue to lead the line with seven goals to his name in 11 caps, while Irankunda is becoming ever more important to his nation's attack with the Sporting Lisbon forward already on 21 caps and seven goals at 20 years of age.

Abunada; Al-Oui, Khoukhi, Miguel, Ahmed; Boudiaf, Madibo, Fathy; Al-Haydos, Ali, Afif

Beach; Circati, Souttar, Herrington; Italiano, Metcalfe, McGree, Behich; Younis, Yengi, Irankunda

Friday's friendly should be a hotly-contested one between two nations with plenty of quality and experience, but we give Australia the slight edge throughout their squad and fancy them to prevail in Doha.

#1633. Egypt vs Malawi - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 11 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 00:09

Egypt begin a new chapter under Ali Maher when they welcome Malawi to Cairo on Friday for round three of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, with the newly appointed head coach having little time to settle in before his first assignment with the national team.

The Pharaohs lead Group B on goal difference after collecting four points from their opening two qualifiers, sitting one point above third-placed visitors.

Maher takes charge of Egypt for the first time following the dismissal of Hossam Hassan on November 7, bringing an abrupt end to his two-year-and-nine-month spell in charge, during which he guided the team to a fourth-placed finish at the 2025 AFCON and qualification for the 2026 World Cup, where they reached the last 16.

Since their defeat to Argentina at the global tournament, the Pharaohs have played three matches, producing a mixture of attacking quality and inconsistency, with the North African side beating South Sudan 5-0 in Juba after opening their qualifying campaign with a goalless draw against Angola.

Hassan's final match in charge was a 1-0 friendly defeat to South Africa in Cairo on October 4, while the Egyptian Football Association cited concerns about the national team's image and stability when announcing the decision to relieve the 60-year-old of his duties.

Although the former coach won 23 of his 39 matches in charge of the Pharaohs (D10, L6), Maher inherits a side that have managed just two victories inside regulation time in their last nine outings, leaving him with the task of bringing greater consistency to the team.

Egypt have also struggled to convince on home soil in recent matches, failing to score in their last two outings in the country, although their record against Friday's opponents offers some encouragement, having won four of their previous six meetings (D1, L1).

Malawi have their own problems to address on the road, having failed to win any of their last five away fixtures, losing three of those matches inside regulation time and failing to score in three.

That poor run reflects the visitors' wider struggles, with Kalisto Pasuwa's side managing just two victories in their last nine outings across all venues (D2, L5), one of which came in the opening round of the AFCON qualifiers when they beat South Sudan 2-1 in Lilongwe.

However, the Flames failed to build on that promising start as they suffered a 3-1 defeat to Angola in their previous qualifier, leaving them under pressure to take something from this encounter, particularly as another loss coupled with an Angola victory would leave them four points behind the qualification places.

The stakes are heightened by Malawi's limited history at the continental tournament, having qualified just three times previously, with their most recent appearance coming in the 2021 edition, when they reached the last 16 for the first time, while Pasuwa has also admitted that securing AFCON qualification will determine his future.

Captain Mohamed Salah is also available again after missing the previous two outings against South Sudan and South Africa, while Trezeguet has returned from injury and Omar Marmoush is expected to feature in the lineup.

#1632. Kai Havertz's offside problem: Arsenal star has been caught astray FIFTEEN times already this season - and even Mikel Arteta admits striker must address his issue - as imperious defence bails champions out again

Published: 02:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 02:26 EST, 8 November 2026

There’s being eager to break through on goal — and then there is Kai Havertz.

Aside from squandered chances, the sight of the Arsenal striker being caught offside at some point in a match this season is an expectation.

Havertz has been penalised for offside 15 times in the Premier League this season, which is seven times more than Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin (in 2nd on eight offsides).

Last season, Bukayo Saka was caught offside 14 times in the league. It is not good enough, and an issue which must be rectified.

A wider scoreline, fronted by Havertz taking his chances, would often change the trajectory of Arsenal matches. Certainly, the 1-0 victory against Hull City on Saturday didn’t need to be so tight.

Mikel Arteta, who can often be defensive of scrutinised players, didn’t even try to mask Havertz’s offside problem afterwards.

Kai Havertz has an issue with repeatedly being caught offside and Mikel Arteta knows he must improve that aspect of his game when leading the line

He said: ‘Yes, it’s something to improve. That's related sometimes to the timing (of the delivery) or really the situation, or the position, where he's lined up and what space he's given. But certainly it's far too many (offsides).

‘I think the sample is quite short to analyse it, but you have a point there. It's a combination. It's all about timing. So there is a signal on the ball, and you need to time it around that.’

A number of deliveries into the final third saw the striker caught out for getting too excited and breaching the backline too early.

The most crucial stray offside against Hull was on the stroke of half-time, Martin Odegaard’s pass aimed in the path of Havertz. As he reached for the ball, Nobel Mendy had grabbed the German’s shirt, tugging him back. A VAR check resulted in referee Farai Hallam announcing that the shirt pull was a foul — but Havertz was offside, meaning no penalty.

It’s a more complex situation, though, than the German simply being too eager in latching onto deliveries.

His team-mates are, on occasion, guilty of not passing to Havertz more sooner. Instead of playing the ball as soon as the opportunity opens up, the delay causes the forward to second-guess himself on when to break ahead.

So the onus is on the Arsenal midfield to time their through balls better, and better understand Havertz’s patterns of play, too. If both elements can click, Havertz and Arsenal’s goal tally will see an uptick.

Otherwise, only the striker’s offside infringement tally will continue to be the beneficiary.

Havertz will latch onto more chances if he is played in at the right time by midfielders

A 1-0 to the Arsenal pattern is already emerging.

Saturday’s victory over Hull was the Gunners’ fifth by such a scoreline across all competitions this season.

The ability to edge matches is a necessary ingredient in a title-winning campaign, particularly in sub-optimal performances.

The Gunners were seriously wasteful in their chances, which better sides will punish. Yet, it’s their ability to carry out wave upon wave of attack, almost expecting the sheer pressure to eventually produce a goal, that is ultimately hard for opponents to resist.

Overall, it’s the north London club’s equal-best start to a league season: 27 points from 10 games, equalling the same tally from their 2022-23 campaign. Their title defence is on the right track — according to the points tallies, anyway.

Arsenal's defence has been integral to their success this season and kept another clean sheet

The Hull City blueprint is a plan other underdog sides should assess when facing Arsenal.

The so-called ‘park the bus’ defensive set-ups are a commonality at the Emirates, owing to the calibre of players both in Arsenal’s starting XI and on their bench.

If a team survives the initial onslaught by the hour mark, Arteta typically turns to the bench and breaks a game open with a change or three.

Here, Piero Hincapie, Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Eberechi Eze all came on before 70 minutes, their fresh legs helping breakdown Hull’s stubborn defence.

Still, the visitors’ high backline is a shrewd set-up which did work to great effect - before Odegaard’s strike.

Arsenal expect inferior sides to sit back, soak up the pressure and mount the odd counter-attack.

By pushing defenders higher up the pitch, it forced Arteta to adapt his carefully laid plans and gave his players a different dimension to navigate, slightly throwing them off track. Manager Sergej Jakirovic deserves his credit.

Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic came up with an excellent strategy that other sides could use

The final word must go to Noni Madueke. He’s received his fair share of scrutiny this season, the winger’s end product an area which is continually brought up.

When in full flow, he is so hard to stop because of his quick feet and directness — which is why more is often expected of Madueke. He is some talent.

Eze, on the bench, was called up by Thomas Tuchel for his latest England squad, with Madueke left out.

On the basis of this, and other recent performances, Madueke has been hard done by.

Though, with Saka sidelined, he can use the next two weeks to ready himself for some huge Arsenal games ahead against Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City and Real Madrid. The opportunity to stake a real claim in Arteta’s side is there for the taking.

#1630. Montserrat vs Nicaragua - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 23:59, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 05:55

With a place in the preliminary round of the 2027 Gold Cup at stake, Montserrat will host Nicaragua for the first leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in showdown at Estadio Cibao, kicking off at midnight UK time on Friday.

The Emerald Boys are in excellent form after four wins on the bounce, while the Blue and White struggled in the group stage, suffering four defeats.

Gabriel Calderon's Montserrat are the underdogs on paper, owing to the fact they are the entrants into this play-in from League C, but they have put together an impressive campaign so far.

The Emerald Boys won all four of their clashes in League C's Group A, topping the table with 12 points after four games and qualifying for this tie as the highest-ranked nation in their league.

Calderon's side kicked off with a 2-0 victory over Turks and Caicos Islands, and after successive 3-0 and 2-0 triumphs against the British Virgin Islands, hammered Turks and Caicos 4-1 on home turf on October 6.

That flawless streak of wins saw Montserrat score 11 times and concede just once, a defensive record that could be crucial on Friday.

However, it remains to be seen whether the 172nd-ranked nation can maintain that level of solidity up against an opponent 35 places better in FIFA's ratings.

Meanwhile, Juan Cruz Real's Nicaragua have endured a dire Nations League term, failing to avoid defeat even once to date.

The Blue and White finished at the bottom of League A's Group A with zero points to their name, and arrive for this first leg having last earned a victory back in November 2025, when they beat Honduras 2-0 in a World Cup qualifier.

Real's men were downed 3-2 by the Dominican Republic on matchday one of the group stage, falling two goals behind within the first 15 minutes, before fighting back to 2-2 only to see Porto's Pablo Rosario snatch the points with a 97th-minute dagger.

That demoralising loss set the tone for Nicaragua, who followed up with a 6-1 battering by Curacao, a 3-0 thrashing by Costa Rica, and another defeat to the Dominican Republic last time out - 2-1 on October 5.

Looking ahead to Friday's showdown, fans of the visitors will be most concerned by the fact their team conceded 14 goals across just four group matches while netting only four of their own.

With that defensive frailty in mind, manager Real will be desperate to avoid accruing a first-leg deficit that may put the tie beyond Nicaragua before they can dig in for the second leg on home turf.

Hoping to keep up their impressive defensive record, Montserrat look set to start Trent Carter-Rogers in goal, shielded by a centre-back partnership of Nico Gordon and Reading's Jeriel Dorsett.

At the opposite end of the pitch, captain Lyle Taylor should be ready to lead the line, joined in a strike partnership by Ashley Boatswain of Gateshead, while being supported from out wide by Brandon Barzey and the versatile Lenni Cirino.

As for Nicaragua, a five-man backline featuring Justing Cano, Marvin Fletes and Juan Luis Perez at its core is likely to operate in front of San Carlos shot-stopper Jason Vega Carmona.

Joab Gutierrez and Emmanuel Gomez are expected to start as the visitors' wingbacks, aiming to provide width for the attack as well as cover for what has been a vulnerable defence so far in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, Jaime Moreno Ciorciari of Finnish side KuPS will line up as a lone striker, aided by Efrain Mejia and Raheem Cole.

Carter-Rodgers; Kirnon, Gordon, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Comley, Dyer, Cirino; Taylor, Boatswain

Vega Carmona; Gutierrez, Cano, Fletes, Perez, Gomez; R Cole, Moncada, K Cole, Mejia; Moreno Ciorciari

Montserrat proved more than capable of dominating opponents during the group stage, and will be confident of continuing that trend this week.

By contrast, Nicaragua will be low on confidence after suffering a number of damaging defeats to this point, and keeping the scoreline down may be their aim for the first leg.

#1629. Opinion: Andoni Iraola has decided what he wants to do with 'very strong' defender

Liverpool have got a lot of decisions to make before the January transfer window opens up.

The Anfield outfit have had a lot of questions asked about the future of their squad with several areas among their ranks still needing to be upgraded.

They may have spent well over £600 million on new players across the last couple of years but, it's still not been enough.

This has caused them to end up fourth in the Premier League which, if we're being honest, is far from ideal.

However, since the winter transfer window is now edging closer, even more decisions will need to be made about the futures of some Liverpool players with Andoni Iraola already making his mind up about one star.

Liverpool may not want to sign Ronald Araujo after Malo Gusto news

In the summer, four new players were brought to Anfield.

All four of them have had a positive impact on the way things have gone in L4 this term with each of them putting on man of the match performances this term.

Of the lot, Ronald Araujo, who has been described as "very strong" in the past, has probably been the most successful.

He's helped solidify the Reds' back line and, without him this season, Iraola's defence would have been tricky to sort out.

However, since he's only on a season-long loan with an option to buy, nobody knows exactly what Liverpool are going to do about his future.

And, thanks to this latest update from TEAMtalk about Malo Gusto, even more questions have been thrown into the mix.

"Malo Gusto is ready to leave Chelsea in the January transfer window, with the club also open to the possibility of his departure, TEAMtalk understands," they wrote.

"Liverpool also made enquiries about the defender in the summer, while Tottenham Hotspur were among the other Premier League clubs to explore his availability.

"Both could yet emerge as potential destinations if Gusto’s situation at Stamford Bridge continues to develop in the coming weeks and particularly with the Reds open to signing a specialist right-back in 2027 owing to their own well-publicised issues with the position and amid doubts that the Reds will fork out to sign Ronald Araujo on a permanent basis.

"However, if Liverpool do press the button on that deal, they will not have things all their own way, with the interest in Gusto not restricted to England, and with several European clubs also keeping tabs on the Frenchman.

"Atletico Madrid, AC Milan, Como and RB Leipzig are among those to have shown an interest, giving Gusto a number of potential routes away from West London.

"Chelsea are aware of the growing interest and are open to the prospect of a January exit."

Malo Gusto being open to leaving Chelsea could cause Liverpool to re-ignite their interest

Right-back is still a problem for Liverpool.

Nobody knows who the Reds' starting full-back is going to be next term and, with Gusto now open to leaving Chelsea, another spanner has been thrown into the works.

Because, on deadline day of the summer transfer window, the Reds made a last-ditch bid for the Frenchman to try and solve their right-back problems.

Indeed, Conor Bradley is due back in the new year but, after spending so much time on the sidelines and after such a serious injury, it's unclear whether he's going to be able to get back to his best or not.

But, with Gusto now being open to leaving and Liverpool's interest well-documented, it could mark the end of the line for Araujo.

Here's hoping that fans receive some sort of clarity soon.

Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include England's clash with Croatia at Wembley, and a contest between Italy and France.

Armenia welcome Cyprus to the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium on Thursday evening for their penultimate League C fixture in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, the Collectives played out a goalless draw with Montenegro at the Podgorica City Stadium, while the Blue and Whites claimed a narrow 2-1 victory over Latvia in Nicosia.

With their form slipping in recent matches and a gap beginning to open up between themselves and the promotion places, it is imperative that Armenia claim all three points against Cyprus if they are to have even the slightest chance of competing in League B when the 2028-29 Nations League campaign gets underway.

However, with the Blue and Whites enjoying a promising run of form and also chasing down Montenegro in the race for automatic promotion, we believe Armenia’s hopes of progressing will run their course on Thursday as the visitors to take all three points in Yerevan.

#1627. CM: Monza CEO confirms interest in nine-goal star Varela – Milan among the suitors

Gustavo Varela is attracting a lot of interest after his start to the season with Monza, and AC Milan have been named as a suitor.

As Calciomercato.com report, Varela is one of the revelations of the season so far, given that he is top scorer in Serie A with nine goals in 10 appearances. Many teams are closely following the former Benfica player’s development, but Monza will not let him go without a fight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Mauro Baldissoni – the CEO of Monza – made this clear when he spoke to Sky from the Social Football Summit in Turin, explaining the position of the club.

“It’s too easy to talk about just one player and too easy to take credit. We did well, but above all, he did well: he was called upon to make a leap, to make an effort, and he did it very well,” he said.

“Now he’s calm and serene, but he knows he hasn’t achieved anything yet. The foundations are there for a great career. The goal is to have him with us until the end of the season. We know he’s being followed by clubs with great ambitions, but we want to keep him as long as possible.

“It’s still mid-November and no real discussions have been had with anyone. We know that the boy has received some interest through his agent and we’ve received some as well. But it’s all very premature.”

Interest has been confirmed, but from whom? Over the past few weeks, the Portuguese has been closely monitored by scouts from various clubs and strongly linked with several Italian big clubs.

Juventus are looking for another centre-forward to give to Spalletti. Milan want a quality alternative to Gonçalo Ramos and are in the hunt, even if Nicolo Tresoldi has been linked. Inter president Beppe Marotta denied the possibility of adding a fifth striker to the squad, but they are always lurking.

Napoli are closely monitoring the situation too. Massimiliano Allegri has outlined his needs for a striker in the summer to replace Lorenzo Lucca (who is set to leave again), so they are among the frontrunners.

Last summer, Monza paid just €2m to acquire him from Benfica and sign him to a contract until 2030. In just two months, his price has skyrocketed and the asking price is now around €25-30m. Selling in January remains unlikely, unless a big offer is forthcoming.

However, there is the Benfica factor. The Portuguese giants have two clauses in their favour: they will get a 20% share of the capital gain on the player’s future resale, and they have the ability to match any offers that may come from other teams.

#1626. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta could enter 'war' with Liverpool for £100m Premier League star in January window

By Lewis Nolan | 12 Nov 2026 00:19

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a January move for Alex Scott but could face competition from Liverpool, the newest report has revealed.

The Gunners have enjoyed a remarkable start to the Premier League season, with the club in first place with 27 points from a possible 30.

Many view Mikel Arteta's side as clear favourites for the title, though the head coach will not be complacent in the race to win the league.

While the Gunners' squad is already strong, their status as title favourites would not be in question should they strengthen in January.

The i Paper claim that Arsenal have made an enquiry to Bournemouth for Scott, who was reportedly priced at £100m in the summer, though other teams like Liverpool have also enquired about him ahead of January and are particularly keen this winter.

Scott will have just a year left on his contract in the summer, meaning January may be the only time left that Bournemouth can extract maximum value for him.

The 23-year-old is an immense passer, with his ability to break opposition lines making him one of the standouts in the division since last season.

Arteta is known to demand significant work from his midfielders without the ball, something that Scott has excelled at for the Cherries.

In fact, the midfielder has won 63% of his ground duels in the Premier League this season, while also recovering the ball 7.2 times per game.

The problem for Arsenal in any race against Liverpool is that they may not have a spot open for him in the middle of the pitch, whereas the Reds will.

Declan Rice is certain to start for the Gunners for as long as he is at the Emirates, but the Londoners have already committed to Bruno Guimaraes.

Arsenal also have Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly in their squad, whereas there are concerns about the future of Alexis Mac Allister at Liverpool, while the performances of Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch have been poor.

If the Merseysiders offer Scott more playing time, then the Gunners may find it difficult to beat their rivals to the midfielder.

#1625. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.
